The code has two type families, and the golden tests compare each format's output with captured output of the replaced Python, not with each other (`../diagram-ir/tests/golden_parity.rs:1-2`). |
| DR-02 | [DI-01.3](diagram-ir/01-the-ir-and-its-input-parsers.md#di-013-where-each-drawio-limit-fires) _(README vs code)_ | the README lists "XML attributes per element" and "XML nesting depth" as "bounded by xmldom" and describes `xmldom` as having attribute and depth limits (`../diagram-ir/README.md:76-77`, `../diagram-ir/README.md:65`). The tree builder pushes onto an unbounded stack and collects every attribute with no count or depth check (`../diagram-ir/src/xmldom.rs:82-130`, `../diagram-ir/src/xmldom.rs:132-149`). The bound that exists is indirect: the inflate cap and the CLI's file cap limit how many bytes can reach the parser. |
| DR-03 | [DI-01.3](diagram-ir/01-the-ir-and-its-input-parsers.md#di-013-where-each-drawio-limit-fires) _(README vs code)_ | the README table lists "Max nodes 2,000" and "Max edges 5,000" beside the draw.io limits (`../diagram-ir/README.md:74-75`). Those are Mermaid constants (`../diagram-ir/src/mermaid/mod.rs:20-21`); draw.io has no node or edge cap, only the cell caps above, which count vertices, edges and edge labels together (`../diagram-ir/src/drawio/model.rs:113-114`). |
| DR-04 | [DI-02.1](diagram-ir/02-analysis-digest-and-json-output.md#di-021-from-arguments-to-the-text-a-reader-gets) _(README vs code)_ | the README describes `pyfmt` as "Python format-string interpolation for template variables" (`../diagram-ir/README.md:64`). The module is Python-compatible `repr`, `splitlines`, `strip`, `bool` and path helpers for the digests, and nothing in it interpolates template variables (`../diagram-ir/src/pyfmt.rs:1-6`). |
| DR-05 | [DI-03.2](diagram-ir/03-the-self-check-and-motion-template-resolution.md#di-032-a-run-of-the-binary-file-by-file) _(README vs code)_ | the README gives exit code 2 as "tool error" for this binary (`../diagram-ir/README.md:127`). The exit paths in `main` itself end in 0 or 1, and the header documents only those (`../diagram-ir/src/bin/self_check.rs:11`, `../diagram-ir/src/bin/self_check.rs:63-67`); a file it cannot read or decode is a `FAIL` entry with exit 1 (`../diagram-ir/src/bin/self_check.rs:43-45`), so the most obvious tool error does not give 2. What status a rejected command line gives is decided by the argument parser, which these sources do not show. |
